text-1mib.why: 1 MiB of paragraphs, 264 pages: the account holds about 49 MiB at its peak.

text-4mib.why: 4 MiB of paragraphs, about 1,050 pages: the account holds about 200 MiB at its peak, the Go heap about 470 MiB.

text-16mib.why: 16 MiB of paragraphs, the default input cap, about 4,200 pages: the account holds about 800 MiB at its peak, under the 1 GiB budget, and the Go heap about 1.7 GiB.

html-1mib.why: 1 MiB of paragraphs, 257 pages: the account holds about 170 MiB at its peak, the Go heap about 390 MiB.

html-4mib.why: 4 MiB of paragraphs, about 1,025 pages: the account holds about 690 MiB at its peak, the Go heap about 1.7 GiB.

html-16mib.why: 16 MiB of paragraphs: the styles, boxes, shaped paragraphs and glyph runs would hold about 2.7 GiB, and the budget refuses them during the layout, a few seconds in.

html-png-10.why: Ten distinct 12-megapixel PNGs: 480 MB of decoded pixels, under the budget, held until the document is written.

html-png-50.why: Fifty distinct 12-megapixel PNGs: 2.4 GB of decoded pixels while every picture is held until the document is written; the budget refuses the picture past 1 GiB before decoding it.

html-jpeg-10.why: Ten distinct 12-megapixel JPEGs, written as they are: no pixel is decoded or charged.

html-jpeg-50.why: Fifty distinct 12-megapixel JPEGs, written as they are: no pixel is decoded or charged.

csv-100k.why: 100,000 cells, 197 pages: the account holds about 180 MiB at its peak, the Go heap about 310 MiB.

csv-1000k.why: 1,000,000 cells, the cap: each cell is charged what the pages built from it cost when it is read, so the budget refuses the workbook while it is read, before any page is planned.

docx-2000pages.why: 2,000 pages of one paragraph each: the account holds about 160 MiB at its peak, the Go heap about 510 MiB.
